verdict.rationale: Cloudflare Workers ships an official command-line tool, Wrangler, for creating, developing, deploying and rolling back Workers. Its docs say it fits GitHub Actions workflows, and scoped API tokens are documented for CI/CD and automation. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of non-interactive Wrangler authentication and deploy steps in CI pipelines (the CI/CD token guidance shown applies to the MCP server), and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: A command line tool for building [Cloudflare Workers](https://workers.cloudflare.com/).
The core Wrangler commands for creating, developing, and deploying Workers are on the Workers commands page.
Fits into your existing workflows: Git, GitHub Actions, VS Code, and any framework.
For CI/CD or automation, you can create a Cloudflare API token with the permissions you need and pass it as a bearer token in the Authorization header.
You can roll back to a previously deployed version of your Worker using Wrangler or the Cloudflare dashboard.
